title: Features | Cancer | CDC
content: Features Aug. 25, 2025 Español What to know These pages provide an overview of cancer topics that are appropriate for the season, or support a health observance. Features Breast Cancer Awareness Ask your doctor when you should get a mammogram. Sept. 25, 2024 Cancer and Men Men have higher rates of getting and dying from cancer than women. Aug. 29, 2024 Cancer and Women You can take steps every day to lower your chance of getting certain kinds of cancer. Nov. 14, 2024 Cancer Prevention Starts in Childhood You can lower your children’s risk of getting cancer later in life. July 1, 2024 Cervical Cancer Awareness You can lower your risk for cervical cancer by getting screened regularly, starting at age 21. Dec. 11, 2024 Colorectal Cancer Awareness Colorectal cancer screening saves lives. June 12, 2024 Gynecologic Cancer Awareness Learn about cancers that start in a woman’s reproductive organs. Aug. 29, 2024 Healthy Living After Cancer These tips can help you stay healthy during and after your cancer treatment. Aug. 29, 2024 Lung Cancer Awareness You can lower your lung cancer risk in several ways. Oct. 15, 2024 Preventing Infections in Cancer Patients Call your doctor right away if you get a fever or feel sick during your chemotherapy treatment. Nov. 14, 2024 Prostate Cancer Awareness Learn about the possible benefits and harms of prostate cancer screening and talk to your doctor. Sept. 12, 2024 Skin Cancer Awareness To lower your skin cancer risk, protect your skin from the sun and avoid tanning. Aug. 29, 2024 World Cancer Day CDC strives for a world where all people are free of cancer.
